title: A flat 1 kHz low-pass filter
story: A sensor signal lives below a few hundred hertz, but it picks up whine at 10 kHz and above. Build a second-order Sallen-Key low-pass filter: two 10 kOhm resistors, a 10 nF capacitor from the op-amp's plus input to ground, and the op-amp as a unity-gain follower. Choose the feedback capacitor (from the middle node to the output) so the filter is flat up to its cutoff near 1 kHz, without a resonant bump.

goals.label: cutoff (-3 dB) between 950 Hz and 1.3 kHz
flat pass band: within 1 dB at 400 Hz
whine at 10 kHz cut by at least 35 dB

hints: For this filter f0 = 1 / (2 pi R sqrt(C1 C2)) and Q = sqrt(C1 / C2) / 2.
A flat (Butterworth) response needs Q = 0.707, so C1 is about twice C2.
Too large a C1 makes Q big: a bump before the cutoff. Too small a C1 makes the filter sag early and gently.
